subject: Imputed data - ordered categorical to continuous

messages.author: a014794d3d3c49fa
messages.subject: Imputed data - ordered categorical to continuous
parts:
Hi

I am running a CFA with data for which multiple imputation was used to compute missing values. Seeing as the input data is actually ordered categorical (likert), I am assuming that the imputed values are likely not integers. Thus, the imputed values are likely to be continuous? Does anyone know how lavaan deals with this, and whether or not its a problem?

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Imputed data - ordered categorical to continuous
parts:
When using multiple imputation (MI) you want your imputation model to match your analysis model. So if in your imputation model the likert items were treated as continuous you would also want to fit your analysis model (in lavaan) treating those items as continuous. If your imputation model treated the likert items as ordered categorical, then you would want to analyze your data in the same way. So the first step is to determine how you want to treat your variables (ordered categorical or continuous) and then determine your imputation and analysis methods from there. 

If you're looking for examples, the help file for runMI in the semTools package has an example of imputing and analyzing categorical data.

Hope this helps,

Alex

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Imputed data - ordered categorical to continuous
parts:
The example in the runMI documentation is missing the code for each model (oops, we'll update for the next version, in the mean time see below for the full example).

In your case, I think the issue is that you specified that the variables are ordered for lavaan but not for mice. In runMI you can use the miArgs argument to pass arguments (as a list) to the imputation routine. With mice to declare all variables as ordinal you would need to include miArgs = list(method = "polyreg") in your call to runMI (or you could use any of the other options mice provides for ordered variables)


library(semTools)

popModel <- "
f1 =~ 0.6*y1 + 0.6*y2 + 0.6*y3 + 0.6*y4
y1 ~*~ 1*y1
y2 ~*~ 1*y2
y3 ~*~ 1*y3
y4 ~*~ 1*y4
f1 ~~ 1*f1
y1 | 0.5*t1
y2 | 0.25*t1
y3 | 0*t1
y4 | -0.5*t1
"


analyzeModel <- "
f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
y1 ~*~ 1*y1
y2 ~*~ 1*y2
y3 ~*~ 1*y3
y4 ~*~ 1*y4
"

dat <- simulateData(popModel, sample.nobs = 200L)
miss.pat <- matrix(as.logical(rbinom(prod(dim(dat)), 1, 0.2)), nrow(dat), ncol(dat))
dat[miss.pat] <- NA
out5 <- cfa.mi(analyzeModel, data=dat, ordered=paste0("y", 1:4), m = 3,
miArgs=list(ords = c("y1", "y2", "y3", "y4")))
summary(out5)
inspect(out5, "fit")
inspect(out5, "impute")

messages.subject: Re: Imputed data - ordered categorical to continuous
parts:
Finally, I made it for simplifying runMI syntax for my laziness and prevent mistakes.

It will be used WLSMV estimator in SEM context; not CFA.

> categoricalMI <- function(model = ..., data = ..., m = ..., ...) {
+   
+   #####################
+   # categorical MI    #
+   #####################
+   # Multiple          #
+   # Imputation for    #
+   # categorical       #
+   # variables         #
+   # in SEM context    #
+   #####################
+   # Seongho Bae       #
+   # seo...@kw.ac.kr  #
+   # Nov 6th 2014      #
+   # Under GNU / GPL   #
+   #####################
+   
+   # checking packages for multiple impuation in SEM context
+   if(!require('semTools')) {
+     try(install.packages('semTools', dependencies = TRUE), silent=TRUE)
+   }
+   
+   if(!require('Amelia')) {
+     try(install.packages('Amelia', dependencies = TRUE), silent=TRUE)
+   }
+   
+   if(!require('lavaan')) {
+     try(install.packages('lavaan', dependencies = TRUE), silent=TRUE)
+   }
+   
+   # loading packages for multiple imputation in SEM context
+   require('semTools')
+   require('Amelia')
+   require('lavaan')
+   
+   fit <- sem(model=model, data=data) # extract variable names in model syntax
+   
+   fit_MI <- runMI(model=model, data=data[,attributes(fit)$Model@dimNames[[1]][[1]]], m=m, fun='sem', ordered=names(data[,attributes(fit)$Model@dimNames[[1]][[1]]]), miArgs=list(ords = attributes(fit)$Model@dimNames[[1]][[1]]), estimator = 'WLSMV', ...)
+   
+   cat(summary(fit_MI, standardize=T))
+   cat(inspect(fit_MI, 'fit'))
+   
+   return(fit_MI)
+ }
> hexaco.fit_MI <- categoricalMI(model=hexaco.model.sem, data=rawdata, m=5)
